problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{C}_{1},-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(\frac{\pi }{4})=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩.$ 
Substituting $t=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+{C}_{1},-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+{C}_{1},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{1} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$
